title: Your body is a temple (1 Corinthians 6:12–20)
hookLine: you are not your own; you were bought with a price
tomorrow: the Corinthians mailed Paul their questions. what did they ask?

cards: "It's my body, my call." People say it about sleep, food, screens, all of it. Corinth had a slogan like that: "All things are lawful unto me".
Some readers think it was a saying going round the church. Paul doesn't throw it out. He finishes it: "but all things are not expedient".
Not everything helps. Then again: "but I will not be brought under the power of any." Free, yes.

teach.b: Some readers hear a second slogan right after: "Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats". The body as a machine: what you do with it never touches the soul.
Paul disagrees: "the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body." The Lord is for the body. That's the surprise.

teach.h: A TEMPLE OF THE HOLY GHOST.
teach.b: Then today's line: "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?" Two days ago the temple was all of you together. Now it comes closer.
"For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's."
So the body isn't a shell or a trophy. It's a place where God lives, and it was paid for. For Paul, in this chapter, that means sexual faithfulness.
Some Christians draw more from the line too: rest, food, care, and respect for other people's bodies as well as their own.

how: Christians turn to 1 Corinthians 6:19–20 in teaching about sexual ethics and care for the body; churches apply it in different ways.

games.q: your cousin says 'your body is a temple' means never eating junk food. what's the fairest answer?
o: Paul's point is sexual faithfulness; some apply it to care too.
yes, Paul wrote it as a food rule for Christians.
no, it's really only about tattoos and piercings.
games.why: 1 Corinthians 6 says the body belongs to the Lord, and Paul applies it to sexual faithfulness. care for the body is an application some Christians make.

practice: Close your eyes and move your attention slowly through your body: feet, hands, shoulders, breath, grading none of it. Where you find tiredness, rest there kindly, the way you'd tend a room where someone you love lives.

wordCard.voice: Your body is a temple. Paul's answer to a church that said the body didn't matter: it does, because God lives there.

orig.note: Greek: body. Paul's word in your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost.

carryVoice: Your line: glorify God in your body. It was bought with a price, tired as it is. Rest well.
